title: [R1] Register, authenticate and keep a secure session
acceptance: A user can register and authenticate;An authenticated session is maintained securely;Preferences can be attributed to an identified member

title: [R2] Create a trip, invite members and manage the roster
acceptance: Duration, budget and radius must be positive;The origin must resolve to curated valid coordinates;The creator becomes organiser and duplicate invitations are ignored;The dashboard shows the roster and submission status;Validation errors identify the offending field without discarding the form

title: [R3] Collect structured preferences and availability
acceptance: Destination types and activities use fixed vocabularies;The budget minimum cannot exceed the maximum;The date start cannot follow the end or be in the past;A valid profile is stored against its member;A member can revise a profile before package selection

title: [R4] Build the group profile, common window and conflict report
acceptance: Submitted date ranges are intersected into a common window;Submitted budgets are aggregated into a group band;An empty date intersection is recorded as a conflict;An incompatible budget is reported rather than silently resolved;Profile revisions trigger recomputation

title: [R5] Eliminate destinations over budget, duration or radius
acceptance: Destinations beyond the permitted radius are removed before ranking;Destinations over the estimated total budget are removed before ranking;Destinations incompatible with duration or common dates are removed before ranking;No survivors returns an empty shortlist with a diagnostic rather than an error

title: [R6] Rank feasible destinations by group-fit score
acceptance: Only candidates surviving hard-constraint filtering are scored;Candidates are ordered by group-fit score;Each shortlist item includes its score and estimated group cost;The persisted shortlist can be revisited

title: [R7] Explain preferences each recommendation meets and misses
acceptance: Each recommendation states which preferences it satisfies;Each recommendation states which preferences it does not satisfy;Principal reasons accompany every recommendation;Fewer than three feasible candidates identifies the binding constraint and alternatives

title: [R8] Generate packages with itemised group and per-person costs
acceptance: Supported transport modes show estimated group cost and travel time;At least three packages differ by accommodation, rooms or transport;Each package itemises onward, return, stay, food, local and activity costs;Costs show group total and per-person figures;Over-budget packages are excluded or clearly flagged

title: [R9] Let the organiser set origin, duration, budget and radius
acceptance: Only the organiser supplies group-level trip parameters;Origin is selected from a geocoded curated hub;Duration is a positive integer in nights;Total budget and radius are positive;Valid parameters are persisted on the trip

title: [R10] Protect preference privacy and hash credentials
acceptance: A preference profile is readable only by its owner;The trip group sees preference data only in aggregate;Credentials are stored as salted hashes and never recoverably;Only planning data is collected;Members can delete their personal data

title: [R11] Persist planning data with referential integrity
acceptance: Users, trips, preferences, packages and itineraries use relational persistence;Referential integrity is enforced between related records;Deleting a trip cascades to members, preferences, packages and itineraries;The administrator can maintain the destination catalogue independently of a release

title: [R12] Generate a grounded day-wise itinerary
acceptance: The model receives verified structured trip facts;The itinerary covers onward travel, destination days and return travel;Group activity interests are represented without unreasonable day lengths;Unverified activities are omitted or marked unverified;The itinerary is persisted and available in trip history

title: [R13] Accept, modify or reject generated output
acceptance: A member can accept generated output;A member can modify, reorder or remove itinerary items;A member can reject generated output;The resulting decision and current version are persisted

title: [R14] Fall back to cached or curated data with provenance
acceptance: The core flow continues when an external provider is unavailable;Cached or curated data substitutes for unavailable live data;Every affected figure visibly identifies its provenance;Fallback figures remain labelled as estimates rather than being omitted

title: [R15] Meet interactive and generation response targets
acceptance: Ninety-five per cent of interactive requests complete in under three seconds;A shortlist completes within ten seconds under normal load;A full itinerary completes within thirty seconds for up to eight members;Preference updates become visible without a manual reload;Repeated provider responses are cached

title: [R16] Mediate external services with caching and quota control
acceptance: All provider calls pass through External Data Integration;The module authenticates with each provider;Provider responses are cached;Provider quota usage is controlled;Curated fallback data substitutes when a provider is unavailable

title: [R17] Adjust fairness across recommendation rounds
acceptance: Successive recommendation rounds apply a fairness adjustment;The same member is not repeatedly under-served;The base scoring function remains valid without the adjustment

title: [R18] Let members vote on shortlisted destinations
acceptance: Members can vote on shortlisted destinations;Voting occurs before package selection;The ranked shortlist remains usable without voting
